_comment: Del 17 — configuration for running Atlas.Api inside docker-compose.yml's own containerized stack (ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Docker, set on the api service in docker-compose.yml). Every hostname below (sqlserver, redis, azurite) is a Compose service name, not localhost — Docker Compose's built-in DNS resolves them automatically for any container on the same compose network, which is exactly why this file exists as a THIRD environment alongside Development and Testing rather than reusing either: appsettings.Development.json points at (localdb)\mssqllocaldb, localhost:6379 and Azurite's default 127.0.0.1 endpoint, none of which are reachable by name from inside another container the way they are from a process running directly on Peter's Windows machine.

BlobStorage._comment: This is Azurite's well-known, publicly documented development account key (the exact same one 'UseDevelopmentStorage=true' expands to internally) — never a real secret. The only difference from appsettings.Development.json is the host in BlobEndpoint: 'azurite' (the compose service name), not Azurite's default 127.0.0.1, since 'UseDevelopmentStorage=true' itself always hardcodes 127.0.0.1 and can't be pointed at a different host.

ServiceBus._comment: Left pointing at the same real Azure namespace as appsettings.Development.json is on purpose, so AddMessaging's fail-fast check ('FullyQualifiedNamespace was not found') doesn't stop the container from starting at all — but publishing will still fail (fail-open, logged and swallowed, see ServiceBusTicketEventPublisher/Del 12) because the container has no az-login credentials of its own. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Del 17 section for why that's a documented gap rather than something Del 17 tries to solve.
